entries.title: Psalms 118:1
segments: This psalm was evidently composed to be sung on the occasion of some national festivity, apparently in connection with a solemn procession to the sanctuary; but the period to which it belongs cannot be certainly determined.  Many refer it to the solemnities connected with the foundation of the second temple.
It might, perhaps, with still more propriety be referred to the dedication of the second temple.

entries.title: Psalms 118:5
segments:
I called; the psalmist speaks here in the name of God's people, and so throughout the psalm. 
 
  Set me in a large place; delivered me from restraints and embarrassments.

entries.title: Psalms 118:7
segments: See; the destruction of my enemies.

entries.title: Psalms 118:9
segments: It is better to trust the Lord than to put confidence in men, however honorable or exalted.

entries.title: Psalms 118:10
segments: Me; the psalmist, as the representative of God's people.

entries.title: Psalms 118:12
segments:
The fire of thorns; which is soon extinguished. 
 
The assaults of the wicked upon God's people, however formidable they may appear in the beginning, will end in their own overthrow.

entries.title: Psalms 118:14
segments: God is the source of defence and of joy to his people, and will not disappoint any who put their trust in him.

entries.title: Psalms 118:18
segments: God afflicts his people, not for their destruction, but for their profit; however great their sufferings, he will in the end deliver them.

entries.title: Psalms 118:20
segments: This gate of the Lord; which led into the sanctuary, the place of his worship; supposed to have been said as the solemn procession reached the sanctuary.

entries.title: Psalms 118:21
segments: My salvation; his deliverer from death.

entries.title: Psalms 118:22
segments:
The stone which the builders refused; originally applied to Israel as despised and rejected by the heathen nations, but chosen of God and exalted by him to the most honorable office: afterwards applied by Christ to himself as rejected by the Jewish builders, but exalted by God to be head over all things to his body the church.  The first application includes the second, since Christ is the head and representative of the true Israel. 
 
  The head-stone; which unites the building together. 
 
In selecting the means and instruments of establishing his kingdom in the world, God acts in a manner very contrary to human wisdom, "that no flesh should glory in his presence."

entries.title: Psalms 118:23
segments: This; which is done in the head-stone.

entries.title: Psalms 118:24
segments: This is the day; the day of salvation to Israel.

entries.title: Psalms 118:26
segments: He that cometh in the name of the Lord; applied by the multitude to Christ with his approbation, when he entered Jerusalem as the King of Israel.

entries.title: Psalms 118:27
segments: Bind the sacrifice; preparatory to offering it as a token of gratitude to God.

entries.title: Psalms 118:28
segments: My God; he not only had a God, but by the spirit of adoption could say, My God.

entries.title: Psalms 118:29
segments: The goodness of God in hearing and and answering the prayers of his people should ever be acknowledged with gratitude, thanksgiving, and praise.
